claims.statement: Diagnostic assessment may resolve a finding, support surveillance, or lead to a recommendation for tissue sampling.
caveats: An assessment category is not interchangeable with pathology truth.

claims.statement: Pathology is produced after tissue sampling or surgery and may inform subsequent treatment or imaging.
caveats: The statement supplies no universal timing window or treatment rule.
This context is general clinical background and is not evidence that open-v2 rows form a complete or deterministic event sequence.
No follow-up interval, interval-cancer policy, outcome definition, or modality-inclusion rule is established.

embed.finding-procedure-recording.title: Public EMBED finding and procedure recording
embed.finding-procedure-recording.summary: Public EMBED documentation distinguishes radiologist-recorded findings from later procedure and pathology information in the classic clinical table.

claims.statement: The public classic-table documentation describes findings as radiologist-recorded observations and procedures as later events linked to a finding.
caveats: This statement does not assert that open-v2 stores both entities in one row.

claims.statement: In the documented classic representation, more than one linked procedure can repeat a finding while procedure details differ.
caveats: Finding-row deduplication must not be transferred to open-v2 without profile-specific evidence.

claims.statement: Public EMBED documentation describes pathology as manually entered after a procedure and attributed back to the originating finding.
caveats: Manual attribution can be incomplete and is not a foreign-key guarantee.

claims.statement: The public documentation warns that pathology may be recorded on a diagnostic study without corresponding attribution to an earlier screening study.
caveats: No frequency, temporal window, or deterministic repair rule is established.
This is EMBED-specific public background, but its classic two-table row layout is not authoritative for open-v2.
The context records provenance and hazards, not a pathology backfill algorithm.

open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.title: Open-v2 assessment and recommendation context
open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.summary: Assessment and recommendation are distinct finding-level fields whose clinical and temporal roles must not be collapsed.

claims.statement: Open-v2 represents imaging assessment and imaging recommendation as separate columns at imaging-finding grain.
caveats: Physical co-location does not make the fields semantically interchangeable.

claims.statement: The released assessment codes identify distinct BI-RADS states and must not be reduced to one simple ordinal scale.
caveats: Code membership alone does not establish workflow validity for a particular exam type.

claims.statement: Recommendation strings come from a loose multi-site MagView reporting schema with expected formatting heterogeneity.
caveats: Preserve the source string rather than imposing a canonical grammar.

claims.statement: Mappings for valid recommendation codes absent from the released legend are currently unknown and require investigation with the MagView reporting teams.
caveats: Do not guess or silently normalize undocumented recommendation codes.

claims.statement: The assessment and recommendation columns in combined_anon are convenience projections, not proof of value equality or contemporaneous availability.
caveats: Use the canonical imaging-finding binding when feature provenance matters.
Do not derive an outcome label from assessment or recommendation without a declared task and temporal anchor.
Public pathway guidance does not establish that open-v2 rows form a complete screening-to-diagnostic sequence.

open-v2.linked-exam-context.title: Open-v2 linked-exam references
open-v2.linked-exam-context.summary: Linked accession fields identify same-episode exams linked at study time, with expected data-quality and release-coverage edge cases.

claims.statement: A linked accession is an optional reference and is not guaranteed to resolve to an open-v2 exam row.
caveats: Treat accession identifiers as opaque and release-scoped.

claims.statement: Multiple imaging-finding or wide rows may reference the same linked exam, so joined exam attributes can repeat at the source grain.
caveats: This is a row-multiplication hazard, not an empirical frequency claim.

claims.statement: The linked-study flag and linked-accession presence are expected to describe the same same-episode linkage, but data-quality edge cases can violate row-wise equivalence.
caveats: Do not use one field as a missing-value repair for the other.

claims.statement: A linked accession identifies a same-episode exam linked at study time; it does not designate a prior or follow-up exam.
caveats: Use the linked exams' study dates for their temporal context.
Linked references describe relationship metadata and are not executable joins.
Release filtering and ordinary data-quality artifacts can leave expected link or flag invariants unsatisfied in edge cases.

open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.title: Open-v2 multimodal finding context
open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.summary: The imaging-finding surface contains mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor families without proving modality presence from descriptor nulls.

claims.statement: Open-v2 imaging_findings_anon exposes distinct mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor columns.
caveats: A shared table surface does not make modality-specific descriptors interchangeable.

claims.statement: Exam modality is represented separately at exam grain and should remain distinct from individual descriptor fields.
caveats: Cross-field modality consistency has not been registered as a validated invariant.

claims.statement: Modality-specific descriptor fields indicate presence or absence of particular finding descriptors and do not establish whether that modality was performed or available.
caveats: Use the separate exam/modality features for modality availability.
Descriptor presence and modality availability are separate questions represented by different features.

open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.title: Open-v2 pathology and procedure context
open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.summary: Pathology findings carry procedure, report, surgery, diagnosis-slot, and severity fields with non-unique links back to imaging.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores pathology findings in a separate pathology-finding-grain table with procedure, report, surgery, and diagnosis fields.
caveats: The table grain does not establish a unique clinical row identity.

claims.statement: The registered pathology-to-imaging association uses accession, finding side, and finding number, but is optional and can match multiple rows in either direction.
caveats: Joining can multiply rows and incomplete tuples require an explicit policy.

claims.statement: The side component of the registered imaging relationship is finding side, not biopsy side.
caveats: Do not substitute bside when following the declared table relationship.

claims.statement: Path1 through path10 are procedure-associated pathology descriptor codes, generally ordered by severity group; slot position, within-group order, and duplicate occurrences are not informative for decision-making.
caveats: Duplicate codes are not intended but may occur and are equivalent to one occurrence.

claims.statement: Pathology descriptor codes observed in open-v2 but absent from the released legend are valid source-system codes with mappings that are currently unknown.
caveats: Retain unknown codes as observed and defer their interpretation to internal MagView mapping investigation.

claims.statement: Pathology severity is the inverse coded group of the most severe attached pathology descriptor: 0 invasive cancer, 1 in-situ cancer, 2 high-risk lesion, 3 borderline lesion, 4 benign finding, and 5 non-breast cancer.
caveats: Lower values are more severe; null means no attached pathology and is not benign or negative.
Procedure and pathology information may postdate imaging and must not be treated as contemporaneous by default.
In the classic MagView representation, distinct procedures carry distinct procedure/pathology values even when the associated finding content is otherwise duplicated.

open-v2.report-context.title: Open-v2 report lifecycle context
open-v2.report-context.summary: Reports are accession-linked records whose sequence orders successive MagView report versions; source heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples and the addendum-flag relationship remains unverified.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores anonymized accession-linked radiology report text with the associated report-creation date and MagView report-version sequence.
caveats: Report content was not read while authoring the catalog.

claims.statement: No tested natural tuple uniquely identifies every report row in the registered open-v2 review.
caveats: The technical export index is not a documented durable report identifier.

claims.statement: MagView increments rseq when a new report version is created; within an accession the minimum represented sequence is earliest and the maximum is latest.
caveats: The specific origin of rseq zero is unknown, but zero participates in the same minimum-to-maximum chronology.
Ordinary source-system and site heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples.

claims.statement: Reports with rseq greater than the accession minimum are expected to be addended versions, but the relationship to imaging addendum_flag has not been manually verified.
caveats: Do not infer that one flag identifies a particular report revision.

claims.statement: Joining report rows to finding-grain tables by accession can multiply both report and finding rows.
caveats: Aggregate or select reports only under an explicit report policy.
Use minimum and maximum rseq for earliest and latest represented report versions; do not rely on tuple uniqueness.
Treat report text as potentially sensitive and do not expose raw values through this context service.

open-v2.risk-context.title: Open-v2 risk-assessment context
open-v2.risk-context.summary: Risk outputs were calculated during clinical care in MagView, but several field variants, percentage formatting, exceptional values, and model versions require internal investigation.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores named IBIS and NCI numeric outputs at risk-assessment grain with patient, accession, and study-date references.
caveats: A released name is not a complete clinical definition.

claims.statement: IBISPOP10, IBISPOPL, and IBIS_TD1 through IBIS_TD4 lack confirmed definitions; percentage-point formatting, meanings of -35, -2, and 100, and the generating NCI and IBIS model versions are also unvalidated.
caveats: Do not infer a probability scale or comparable range from numeric physical type.

claims.statement: The risk-to-exam relationship is optional and does not establish that every exam has a risk record.
caveats: No empirical coverage measurement belongs in this catalog.

claims.statement: The released risk scores were calculated during clinical care and extracted from the breast-imaging MagView EHR system.
caveats: Clinical-time calculation does not by itself establish the exact calculation timestamp within the study episode.
Risk output and BI-RADS assessment are different constructs and must not be substituted for one another.
No field is approved for modeling or release merely because it appears in risk_anon.

open-v2.temporal-availability-context.title: Open-v2 temporal availability guardrail
open-v2.temporal-availability-context.summary: Open-v2 dates use a consistent per-patient random shift, preserving within-patient ordering and date differences while obscuring absolute calendar dates.

claims.statement: Open-v2 exposes exam, procedure, and pathology-report date fields in separate clinical surfaces.
caveats: Absolute calendar values are anonymized and must not be interpreted literally.

claims.statement: EMBED applies one consistent random date shift per patient across that patient's dates, so within-patient ordering and date differences are reliable while absolute day, month, and year are not.
caveats: Do not compare absolute calendar dates across patients.

claims.statement: Co-location of fields in combined_anon does not establish that they were observed at the same clinical time.
caveats: The wide table's construction remains unresolved.
Task-specific cohort, follow-up, label, and modality-inclusion choices are analysis policies rather than dataset claims and belong outside this context catalog.
